title: Injectivity in the lowest unknown degree
statement:
Let $g:Y'\to Y$ be a morphism and $n$ an integer invertible on $Y$. Recall that
$\mathrm{BC}(g,n,r)$ means: for every scheme $T$ over $Y$, every qcqs morphism $Z\to T$,
every sheaf of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules $M$ on $Z_{\mathrm{\acute et}}$ and every
$0\leq i\leq r$, the degree-$i$ exchange map ([sk-def-exchange]) for the square with base
change $Y'\times_YT\to T$ and direct image along $Z\to T$ is an isomorphism.

Suppose $q\geq1$ and $\mathrm{BC}(g,n,q-1)$ holds. For every square
obtained by base change as in the definition of $\mathrm{BC}$ and every
sheaf of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules $M$ on $Z_{\mathrm{\acute et}}$, the degree-$q$ exchange map
$b_M^q\colon g^{-1}R^qf_*M\to R^qf'_*u^{-1}M$ is injective. An inclusion
$M\hookrightarrow N$ induces

$$
 \operatorname{coker}(b_M^q)
   \hookrightarrow\operatorname{coker}(b_N^q).
$$

For an embedding $M\hookrightarrow I$ with $I$ injective in the
category of étale sheaves of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules, this cokernel
embeds into $R^qf'_*u^{-1}I$.

*Complement.* In the notation of [sk-def-bc] (smooth side $f$, qcqs side $g$), the same holds
for an arbitrary commutative ring $\Lambda$ in place of $\mathbf Z/n$:

Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, let $q\ge1$ and assume
$\mathrm{BC}(f,\Lambda,q-1)$ of [sk-def-bc] holds. Then for every square
as there (with $g$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated) and every sheaf
$\mathcal F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $T_{\Et}$:

1. the base-change map
$f^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal F\to R^qh_*e^{-1}\mathcal F$ is *injective*;
1. if $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal G$ with $\mathcal G$ a sheaf of
$\Lambda$-modules, the cokernel for $\mathcal F$ is contained in the cokernel for
$\mathcal G$;
1. if moreover $\mathcal G$ is an injective sheaf of
$\Lambda$-modules, that cokernel is contained in
$R^qh_*e^{-1}\mathcal G$.

Consequently a failure of $\mathrm{BC}(f,\Lambda,q)$ is witnessed by a nonzero
element of the cokernel in the stalk at a geometric point of $X$.

proof.text:
Choose $0\to M\to I\to Q\to0$ with $I$ as in the statement. The long
exact sequences give exact rows in

$$
\begin{array}{ccccccc}
g^{-1}R^{q-1}f_*I&\to&g^{-1}R^{q-1}f_*Q&\to&g^{-1}R^qf_*M&\to&0\\
\downarrow{\scriptstyle\sim}&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle\sim}&&\downarrow&&\downarrow\\
R^{q-1}f'_*u^{-1}I&\to&R^{q-1}f'_*u^{-1}Q&\to&R^qf'_*u^{-1}M&\to&R^qf'_*u^{-1}I.
\end{array}
$$

The first two vertical arrows are isomorphisms by
$\mathrm{BC}(g,n,q-1)$, so a diagram chase proves injectivity and the
last assertion. Choosing an injective containing $N$ and comparing the
two diagrams gives the inclusion of cokernels. This is
[Stacks, Tag 0F03](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F03).

*Complement.* The same argument, written for sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules in the notation
of [sk-def-bc], runs as follows.

*Step 1 (embed in an injective).* Choose a short exact sequence
$0\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal I\to\mathcal Q\to0$ with $\mathcal I$ an
injective sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $T_{\Et}$. An injective object
is its own injective resolution, so $R^qg_*\mathcal I=0$ for $q>0$.

*Step 2 (compare the two long exact sequences).* The functors
$f^{-1}$ and $e^{-1}$ are exact, so applying $f^{-1}R^\bullet g_*$ to
the sequence and $R^\bullet h_*$ to its $e^{-1}$-image gives two exact
rows, and the base-change maps of [sk-def-bc] are natural, hence give
the vertical arrows of

$$
\begin{array}{ccccccc}
f^{-1}R^{q-1}g_*\mathcal I&\to&f^{-1}R^{q-1}g_*\mathcal Q&\to&
f^{-1}R^{q}g_*\mathcal F&\to&0\\
\downarrow&&\downarrow&&\downarrow&&\\
R^{q-1}h_*e^{-1}\mathcal I&\to&R^{q-1}h_*e^{-1}\mathcal Q&\to&
R^{q}h_*e^{-1}\mathcal F&\to&R^{q}h_*e^{-1}\mathcal I .
\end{array}
$$

The top right entry is $f^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal I=0$ by Step 1, so the top
row exhibits $f^{-1}R^qg_*\mathcal F$ as the cokernel of its left map.
The two left-hand verticals are isomorphisms by
$\mathrm{BC}(f,\Lambda,q-1)$, so that cokernel is identified with the cokernel
of the bottom left map, which is the image of
$R^{q-1}h_*e^{-1}\mathcal Q\to R^qh_*e^{-1}\mathcal F$. The middle
vertical is therefore the inclusion of that image: this is (1).

*Step 3 (the cokernel).* Exactness of the bottom row continues the
identification: the quotient of $R^qh_*e^{-1}\mathcal F$ by that image
injects into $R^qh_*e^{-1}\mathcal I$, which is (3). For (2), run the
same diagram for $0\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal G/\mathcal F\to0$
with $\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal I$; the
degree-$(q-1)$ isomorphisms again give the inclusion of the cokernel for
$\mathcal F$ into the one for $\mathcal G$.

*Step 4 (a failure is a cokernel element at a point).* By (1) the
base-change map is an isomorphism if and only if its cokernel vanishes,
and a sheaf vanishes if and only if all its stalks do; so if
$\mathrm{BC}(f,\Lambda,q)$ fails there is a geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$
and an element of $(R^qh_*e^{-1}\mathcal F)_{\bar x}$ outside the image.

This is Stacks, Étale Cohomology, Lemma 59.88.2
([`0F03`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F03)).
